preamble: A high back rounded vowel next to another vowel often loses its syllabicity and becomes the labial-velar glide [w], which resolves the hiatus. The process is productive in Spanish and French verb paradigms, where stem-final /u/ becomes [w] when an unstressed vowel-initial ending follows. It is also the regular fate of Bantu noun-class prefixes *mu- before vowel-initial stems.

examples.note: Unstressed /u/ before a vowel is realized as the glide [w], while stressed /u/ stays syllabic in hiatus.
Stem-final /u/ becomes [w] before the vowel-initial infinitive ending. Careful speech can keep the hiatus [lu.e].
The prefix vowel desyllabified to [w] before the vowel-initial stem, as in all class 1 and class 3 prefixes before vowel stems (m(u)- > mw-).

sources: Hualde, J. I. (2005). The Sounds of Spanish. Cambridge University Press.
